meta.title: VPN pricing and plans
meta.description: What a GnomeVPN subscription costs: monthly or discounted over a longer period. Paid by card, with a refund within fourteen days.

title: Pricing
intro: One plan, every server. The longer the term, the cheaper the month. Pay by card and turn auto-renewal off whenever you like.

oneplan.title: One plan rather than several
oneplan.body: We do not split access into tiers: there is no separate price for "fast" servers or for particular countries. Any subscription opens every location and both protocols — Hysteria2 and VLESS + Reality. Only the term differs, and a longer one costs less per month. It is built that way because tiering usually serves the sales funnel rather than the user: the entry plan is made deliberately awkward to push you towards the expensive one.

devices.title: How many devices
devices.body: Two simultaneous connections by default. There is one subscription link — add it to a phone, a laptop and a television, and two of them run at a time. If you need more, extra devices are bought in your account without changing plan. What counts is active connections rather than installations: the app sitting on a fourth device costs you nothing until you use it.

payment.title: Paying and renewing
payment.body: By card on the site, through YooKassa. Access opens the moment the payment clears — the app sees the new expiry on its next subscription refresh, usually within a few minutes. Auto-renewal is one switch in your account: access stays until the end of the period you paid for, and nothing is charged after that.

refund.title: A refund within fourteen days
refund.body: If the service does not suit you, email us within two weeks of paying and we refund the unused period — no interrogation, no request to explain yourself. That is not a marketing line: a VPN cannot be judged from a description, because it behaves differently on different networks, and the only way to know is to try it on your own connection.

expiry.title: What happens when it ends
expiry.body: The subscription does not renew itself once you have turned auto-renewal off. When the term expires, connections stop passing authentication — usually within a few hours of the period ending. Your account and your link survive: to come back you only pay again, and nothing has to be set up on your devices a second time.
